options.plan: Staging; upstream workforce provisioning entitlement unverified
options.region: No WorkOS or upstream region selected; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Org-bound Entra SCIM directory; bearer auth; assigned users/groups; objectId/externalId; app-owned Events API; no login

conditions: Select an organization-bound Entra ID SCIM directory in WorkOS staging and an Entra workforce enterprise provisioning app; use Automatic provisioning with the WorkOS endpoint and bearer token. OAuth client credentials are outside this selected configuration, not declared unsupported.

Enable user/group mappings, map objectId to externalId and select only assigned users/groups as the provisioning scope. Establish this provisioning identity separately from any OIDC sub or JIT account; this is not Entra External ID, B2C or a Graph pull connector.

WorkOS staging connections are not billed per https://workos.com/docs/authkit/environments; production Directory Sync is charged per connection at https://workos.com/pricing. Upstream provisioning entitlement remains unverified; this is not free production or a zero-cost guarantee.

The application requires an Events API bridge with persisted cursor, replay handling and state reconciliation per https://workos.com/docs/events/data-syncing/events-api. WorkOS directory data is read-only to the app, not a native SaaS SCIM endpoint or write-back path; local authorization and sessions remain application-owned.

Scheduled provisioning and on-demand actions are distinct; neither proves immediate end-to-end revocation. This is a dated documentation proposal, not a tested connector or deployed bridge; login/JIT and complete lifecycle enforcement remain unverified.

evidence.summary: The Entra guide documents an organization directory, provisioning credentials, objectId/externalId mapping and assigned-user/group scope. Its scheduled and on-demand paths are not measured application revocation.

conditions: Enable group mappings and explicitly assign groups to the Entra provisioning application; OIDC group claims are not this SCIM group lifecycle. Group externalId is recorded as WorkOS idp_id, unlike Okta's display-name identifier.

Reactivation after directory-level soft deletion may not restore memberships automatically; the guide calls for Restart Provisioning. Verify recovery and reconcile group state instead of assuming reactivation restores all access.

Handle dsync.group.deleted without expecting per-member dsync.group.user_removed events per https://workos.com/docs/directory-sync/understanding-events; remove that group's access without deleting unrelated memberships or user accounts.

The app-owned bridge must reconcile memberships and enforce its own permissions/sessions. This proposal covers configured group ingestion in the selected staging directory, not nested groups, login claims, production entitlement or measured revocation latency.

evidence.summary: The guide documents assigned group provisioning, externalId-based group identity and reactivation caveats. These conditions do not prove complete membership restoration or application access enforcement.
